title: Sent to Europe: architecture, then the bass his father chose
summary: His father sends the children to Italy for schooling; Rudy stays ten years, drops architecture and is made to take up the bass fiddle. His father was stage bandmaster with the Chicago Opera Company.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Until I was about seven, seven and a half, something like that. And then my father decided that he was doing pretty well financially, which he was. So he thought that he would give his children an education in Europe. And since he knew people in Italy, you know, having been born there, he just sent us over there. And, well my sister was the first one to leave. I think she came back to the States after two or three years. And my brother just about the same time. But actually I was the one who stayed the longest of all. I stayed ten years. And what did you study in Europe? Music. Mainly, but before that I studied a little architecture. And that didn't pan out so well for some reason or other. Can't you add? No, actually it had to do with geometry a lot, you know. But that wasn't the reason the reason I was because I was always getting in trouble with the other students. And finally I just got kicked out of the school. So you went into music, huh? Yeah. Or rather my father made me go into music. One day he brought home a bass fiddle and said, this is it for you. And that's been it for me ever since.
